cues.en: A topic that is really under-represented in recommender system research is dealing with the effects of time.
cues.zh: 推薦系統研究中，有個關注度明顯不足的主題，就是時間的影響。

cues.en: One example is seasonality.
cues.zh: 一個例子是季節性。

cues.en: Some items, like Christmas decorations, only make for good recommendations just before Christmas.
cues.zh: 有些項目，例如聖誕裝飾品，只有在聖誕節前推薦才合適。

cues.en: Recommending bikinis in the dead of winter is also a bad idea.
cues.zh: 在嚴冬推薦比基尼，也不是好主意。

cues.en: Picking up on annual patterns like this is hard to do, and most recommender systems won't do it automatically.
cues.zh: 這類年度模式很難捕捉，大多數推薦系統不會自動處理。

cues.en: As far as I know, this is still an open problem in the research arena.
cues.zh: 據我所知，這仍是研究領域中的開放問題。

cues.en: Those of you looking for a master's thesis topic, there you go.
cues.zh: 如果你正在找碩士論文題目，這就是一個。

cues.en: But, something you can do more easily and more generally is taking the recency of a rating into account.
cues.zh: 不過，一個更容易且更通用的做法，是把評分的新近程度納入考量。

cues.en: Netflix in particular found that these sorts of temporal dynamics are important, your tastes change quickly, and a rating you made yesterday is a much stronger indication of your interest
cues.zh: Netflix 特別發現，這類時間動態很重要。你的品味改變得很快，昨天給的評分，比一年前的評分，

cues.en: than a rating you made a year ago.
cues.zh: 更能強烈反映你的興趣。

cues.en: By just weighting ratings by their age, using some sort of exponential decay, you can improve the quality of your recommendations in many cases, or you can use rating recency as a training feature of its own,
cues.zh: 只要依評分的時間遠近加權，例如使用某種指數衰減，很多情況下就能改善推薦品質；也能除了評分本身之外，把評分的新近程度，

cues.en: in addition to the rating itself.
cues.zh: 作為獨立的訓練特徵。

cues.en: As we mentioned in the context of Amazon, the product you're looking at right now is the most powerful indicator of your current interest.
cues.zh: 就像談 Amazon 時提過的，你此刻正在看的產品，是目前興趣最強的指標。

cues.en: Time plays a big part there, as well.
cues.zh: 時間在這裡也扮演重要角色。

cues.en: Whenever you train a recommender system using historical ratings data, you are giving your system a bias toward the past.
cues.zh: 只要使用歷史評分資料訓練推薦系統，就是讓系統帶有偏向過去的偏差。

cues.en: A Netflix that didn't take time into account would end up recommending a lot of old shows to you instead of the hot, newer ones you want to see.
cues.zh: 如果 Netflix 不考慮時間，最後可能推薦很多老節目，而非你想看的熱門新節目。

cues.en: If the things you're recommending are time-sensitive in any way, it makes sense to use rating recency as a training feature of its own.
cues.zh: 如果推薦的東西具有任何時效性，將評分的新近程度作為獨立訓練特徵，就很合理。

cues.en: I could keep on going with real-world lessons, but I'll end with this one.
cues.zh: 我可以繼續講很多實務經驗，但最後用這一點作結。

cues.en: In the real world, a recommender system you're building for a company will ultimately exist for the purpose of driving their profit.
cues.zh: 實務上，你替公司建立的推薦系統，最終目的是推動公司獲利。

cues.en: You may find yourself being asked to optimize your recommender system for profit, instead of pure relevance.
cues.zh: 你可能會被要求，針對利潤最佳化推薦系統，而非只追求相關性。

cues.en: What does that mean?
cues.zh: 這是什麼意思？

cues.en: Well, normally you'd test different recommender systems based on what drives the most purchases, video views, or some other concrete measure of whether a customer liked your recommendation enough
cues.zh: 通常，你會測試不同推薦系統，看哪個能帶動最多購買、影片觀看，或其他具體指標，判斷顧客是否喜歡推薦到足以，

cues.en: to act on it.
cues.zh: 採取行動。

cues.en: If you're trying to build a recommender system that introduces people to new stuff they want, then that's the right thing to do.
cues.zh: 如果想建立一個推薦系統，把人們想要的新事物介紹給他們，這就是正確的做法。

cues.en: You'd want to just optimize on the quantity of items your recommender system drove the consumption of, not how much money those items made for the company.
cues.zh: 你要最佳化的只是推薦系統帶動的項目使用數量，而非那些項目替公司賺了多少錢。

cues.en: But in the real world, some items are more profitable than others.
cues.zh: 但在真實世界，有些項目比其他項目更有利潤。

cues.en: Some items might even be offered at below cost as loss leaders to attract people to your site, and recommending them actually costs your company money.
cues.zh: 有些項目甚至低於成本販售，作為吸引人們到網站的引流商品；推薦它們，實際上會讓公司花錢。

cues.en: This presents a bit of a moral quandary for developers of recommender systems.
cues.zh: 這對推薦系統開發者而言，是一種道德兩難。

cues.en: Do we keep our algorithms pure and optimize only for users' interests, or do we work profit into the equation by rewarding algorithms that generate more profit?
cues.zh: 要維持演算法的純粹，只為使用者興趣最佳化，還是把利潤納入，獎勵能帶來更多利潤的演算法？

cues.en: The euphemism for this is value-aware recommendations, where the contribution to the company's bottom line plays a role in whether something is recommended.
cues.zh: 這被委婉稱為價值感知推薦，也就是某項目對公司獲利的貢獻，會影響它是否被推薦。

cues.en: If you're ever faced with this dilemma, a reasonable compromise is to only use profitability as a tie-breaker.
cues.zh: 如果面臨這種兩難，合理的折衷是只把獲利能力當作平手時的決勝因素。

cues.en: If you're showing top-10 recommendations to someone, and the underlying scores for the top two items in that list are about the same, it wouldn't do any harm to show the more profitable item first.
cues.zh: 如果向某人顯示前十名推薦，清單前兩個項目的底層分數差不多，把利潤較高的項目先顯示，並無大礙。

cues.en: Items higher in a list are more likely to be clicked on, we call this position bias, and if you're really not sure which item should come first, you may as well go with the one that will earn more money for your company.
cues.zh: 清單中位置越高，越容易被點擊，這叫做位置偏差。如果真的不確定哪個該排前面，不妨選能替公司賺更多錢的那個。

cues.en: Optimizing too much for profit can backfire, though.
cues.zh: 不過，過度針對利潤最佳化，可能適得其反。

cues.en: You don't want to end up only recommending expensive items to your customers, because they'll be less likely to purchase them.
cues.zh: 你不會希望最後只向顧客推薦昂貴項目，因為他們會比較不願意購買。

cues.en: It might make more sense to look at profit margin, and not actual profit, so the cost of the item isn't really a factor in what you recommend.
cues.zh: 看利潤率，而非實際利潤，可能更合理，讓項目價格不會真正成為推薦的決定因素。
